origins.section: 9.4 The Answer Waits for the Commit
9.5 A Transaction Holds Its Connection From `Open` to `Close`
9.3 Write in `prepare`, So the Database Can Still Say No
9.7 A Stored Card Number Can Be Found Only With a Key

gates.says: all 4 of this quiz's answerable readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-close-after-send: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-close-after-send: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-close-after-send: 9.4 states that with TX set and Close declared after SendResponse no purchase is answered at all, approved or declined, because SendResponse always runs while the transaction is open.
recorded.prompt:q-pool-and-pause: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-pool-and-pause: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-pool-and-pause: 9.5 shows the same pattern with 4 sessions and 4 connections: PAUSE gives sessions back, paused transactions keep their connections through the Context, new transactions' Open gives up after the 1 s connection-timeout and answers 96; the question's 12 sessions, 30 purchases and 3 s pause carry this over by analogy.
recorded.prompt:q-row-lock-wait: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-row-lock-wait: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-row-lock-wait: 9.3 says the conditional UPDATE locks the row until Close and the second UPDATE waits for the first commit, and 9.5 says a second purchase on the same terminal waits out the first's issuer call, so ~4 s wait plus its own 4 s call gives ~8 s, approved since the limit covers both.
recorded.prompt:q-stolen-backup: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-stolen-backup: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-stolen-backup: 9.7 shows a SHA-256 of a PAN with the known card range and last four is reversed by hashing the ~100,000 Luhn-valid candidates in about a quarter of a second, and every card in the table can be recovered the same way.

gates.says: all 12 of this quiz's discriminating readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-close-after-send:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-close-after-send:a: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-close-after-send:a: 9.4 shows 2.1.7 calls commit in declaration order, so SendResponse runs before Close removes TX and refuses to send; 'both answered' is refuted.
recorded.prompt:q-close-after-send:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-close-after-send:c: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-close-after-send:c: 9.4: Close removes TX only in its own commit, which runs after SendResponse's commit when Close is declared below it, so the approval is withheld.
recorded.prompt:q-close-after-send:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-close-after-send:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-close-after-send:d: 9.4 says 'approved or declined' are both unanswered, and the 9.2 abort trace shows abort also runs in declaration order, so SendResponse refuses the decline before Close's abort removes TX.
recorded.prompt:q-pool-and-pause:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-pool-and-pause:a: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-pool-and-pause:a: 9.5 shows that one connection per session is not enough with PAUSE: with 4 connections, 4 of the 8 purchases got 96.
recorded.prompt:q-pool-and-pause:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-pool-and-pause:b: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-pool-and-pause:b: 9.5 says that after a second the pool gave up and Open answered 96, so Open does not wait for a paused transaction to give its connection back.
recorded.prompt:q-pool-and-pause:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-pool-and-pause:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-pool-and-pause:d: 9.5 says PAUSE gave each session back so more transactions started; the shortage is of connections, not sessions.
recorded.prompt:q-row-lock-wait:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-row-lock-wait:a: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-row-lock-wait:a: 9.3/9.8: the row stays locked until Close commits, so the second UPDATE cannot read past it and go on; it waits.
recorded.prompt:q-row-lock-wait:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-row-lock-wait:c: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-row-lock-wait:c: 9.3: after the wait the second UPDATE re-checks used + amount <= daily_limit, and the stem says the limit has room for both, so it reserves rather than returning 0 and 61.
recorded.prompt:q-row-lock-wait:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-row-lock-wait:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-row-lock-wait:d: 9.3 shows the second UPDATE waited for the lock rather than failing at once; partly true in that 9.3 says a lock timeout in that statement becomes a 96, but not 'at once'.
recorded.prompt:q-stolen-backup:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-stolen-backup:b: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-stolen-backup:b: 9.7's PanProtector.decrypt needs encKey; the IV is stored in the row (iv || ciphertext || tag) and decrypts nothing on its own, though the lesson never states 'the IV is not secret' in words.
recorded.prompt:q-stolen-backup:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-stolen-backup:c: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-stolen-backup:c: 9.7 refutes the conclusion because the unkeyed hash column gives the numbers away; the premise (the key never leaves the HSM, so the ciphertext is safe) is true, making this partly true.
recorded.prompt:q-stolen-backup:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-stolen-backup:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-stolen-backup:d: 9.7 shows the hash is reversed by brute-forcing the few candidates; partly true in that equal hashes do reveal which purchases share a card, but 'only' and 'can't be turned back' are refuted.
